entries.title: A tent for the night
entries.text: Personal notes can now mark a Camping spot with a tent, kept apart from mob camps. Like ore, wood and herb spots, camping spots stay in your own notes. Thanks to James-McMenamin for the idea and the first version.

entries.title: Missing buildings drawn
entries.text: Six places the maps had left blank are now drawn: the stable north of Red Mantle Camp in Fallen Pass (with its stablemaster and stablehand), the Stables cave on Fallen Watch's first level, and the stables of Ail'Vorith, Penshaw in Keeper's Bight, Evershade Weald and the Underdocks.

entries.title: One marker per traveller
entries.text: Adding someone the map already shows now points you to the existing marker so you can update it instead, and five doubled markers were merged. Ore, wood and herb spots stay in your own notes, Ctrl+F (Cmd+F) jumps to search, and Change and Remove sit with Copy link.

entries.title: Grain Cellar stair redrawn
entries.text: The Grain Cellar now has two floors. The entrance stair climbs from the corner of the octagonal hall to the passage under the granary door, all where it really runs; switch floors at the middle landing.

entries.title: Sunken Resort is charted
entries.text: Beneath a Scarwood lake, the flooded halls of Sunken Resort join the atlas across four floors. Follow the bowl-room stairs and the well down to the wisp and elemental caves, find the two air pockets, and turn the new relief view to see how the floors stack.

entries.title: Glinting Hollow is charted
entries.text: The six fae hollows behind the druid portal of the Evershade Weald are on the atlas: the pine forest, the lily pond, the firepits under the great web, the snowy brazier grove, the ice ring and the glowing mushroom ruins. Step through the portal sign in the Weald to visit them.

entries.title: The Great Cavern Sea darkens
entries.text: The waters of the Great Cavern Sea are charted again in the deep, still navy of the other Deep waters, a new little dock appears on the islet where the ship moors, and the road to Ail'Vorith is now marked at the gate itself, under its glowing rune.

entries.title: Quest givers get their own pin
entries.text: The folk who hand out tasks now wear a Quest NPC pin, a figure with an exclamation mark, with its own filter in the Search menu. Over seventy of them across the atlas have been re-pinned; quest spots such as Tig's measuring markers keep the Quest pin.

entries.title: The Caves of Irem, retouched
entries.text: Fresh survey corrections on the Caves of Irem chart: the boat passage at the Great Cavern Sea gate is open water again, the gate's buried walls and stray rock seams are gone, the Giant Den's rim reads as solid rock with the Skri'Var huts now in view, and a few flat-topped columns and a crooked platform were redrawn true.

entries.title: Night Harbor: a back way out of Blackfeather
entries.text: The Eastern sand terraces under Blackfeather now show the ramp and passage that lead out to the North Gate yard, with a sign at the opening. The rock that was drawn across the exit is gone, so the way out reads as open sand.

entries.title: Shallow Shoals is charted
entries.text: The island sea between Keeper’s Bight and Fallen Pass now has its own map: Zaedin’s Landing with its bank and merchants, Black Shoals Fortress, Pirate Island, Player Island and the smaller islands, with clear shallows over the sand shelf. Its exits lead to Keeper’s Bight, the Vale of Zintar and Fallen Pass, and the boat between Keeper’s Bight and Night Harbor now shows its Shallow Shoals stop.

entries.title: The Caves of Irem charted
entries.text: A new chart of the Caves of Irem: the buried sea beneath the Shaded Dunes, the glowing Bluecaps and Redcaps, the Pyramid Complex, the Cave of 1000 Eyes and the Green Lake. Its passages now lead on to the Great Cavern Sea, the Underdocks, the Shaded Dunes, the Ancient Crypt and the Tomb of the Last Wyrmsbane, and the Deep boat's board shows where it sails through.

entries.title: Shared notes join the map
entries.text: A note you shared that is now on the public map no longer stays behind as a second, personal pin: the next time you open that map signed in, it is folded into the public marker. Anything you wrote that the marker does not say is kept as your private note on it. Notes still waiting for review stay yours as before.

entries.title: Faelindral's people on the right board
entries.text: The Wanted notices for folk who live up in Faelindral, such as the guild captains and the scouts of Sentinel's Terrace, now hang on Faelindral's board instead of the Evershade Weald one, and those found at the foot of a lift or by the stables moved down to the Weald. Anyone already marked on either map no longer has a notice on the other.

entries.title: Tidier camp cards
entries.text: Resting the pointer on a camp shows its levels and first mobs; a click opens the full card, with the camp's top five drops at the end. Long cards scroll with a visible bar while their buttons stay in place.

entries.title: Areas and paths
entries.text: A marker can now cover an area (a rectangle, a circle or any outline) or follow a path, such as a camp's grounds or a guard's patrol round. It keeps its type and details, and shapes on the public map go through review like any other change.

entries.title: Your own notes on any place
entries.text: Every marker and place name has a "Your note" box only you can see, kept with your account. Your personal markers now wear a dashed border, and moving a public place sends it for review instead of only moving it in your browser.

entries.title: Smaller fixes
entries.text: Add a personal note and Edit now sit at the top of the Search menu, your notes stay in step across several browsers, and the notices panel no longer runs off the edge of maps shown on other sites.

entries.title: Camp levels and mobs restored
entries.text: A few camps lost the levels and mob lists travellers had given them; they are back, and changes that were sent back for a second look can now be accepted again.

entries.title: Suggesting changes, made simpler
entries.text: Every marker and sign has one Change form with the same fields, the changes on their way show under its name, and the bell at the top lists what's new on the atlas and where your own suggestions stand.

entries.title: Mob camps list their mobs
entries.text: Camps show their level range, the mobs found there with a link to each one's wiki page, and the loot they drop together. Named mobs show their level too.

entries.title: A quick look on hover
entries.text: Rest the pointer on a marker to see what it is before clicking, and long lists such as vendor kinds and destinations can be searched by typing.

entries.title: Safer publishing of travellers' changes
entries.text: Several changes to the same place no longer overwrite each other, an accepted change can no longer be lost on its way to the atlas, and every traveller who improved a place stays credited.

entries.title: Lifts, bridges and stairways as travel seals
entries.text: Between Evershade Weald and Faelindral, lifts, bridges and stairways are now round seals with an up or down mark; their popup takes you to the matching spot on the other map. Two signs that led nowhere were taken down in the Underdocks and Keeper's Bight.

entries.title: Harbour signs show departures
entries.text: Each boat dock lists its sailing times and stops, from Night Harbor to Keeper's Bight and down in the Deep.

entries.title: Surface and the Deep in the map picker
entries.text: Maps are grouped by where they lie, with dungeons and cities marked, and travel signs show lifts, stairs, bridges, ladders and teleporters.

entries.title: World maps redrawn
entries.text: The surface and the Deep follow the official layout; click a zone to fly into it.

entries.title: Vendors say what they sell
entries.text: Filter vendors by their wares from the Search menu.

entries.title: Wiki cards and the Wanted board
entries.text: Markers link to their wiki page, NPCs show a wiki card, and each map's Wanted board lists the NPCs it is still missing.
